yourhonor: Calibrate Large Language Model Judges

Source: R/yourhonor-package.R
yourhonor-package.Rd

Treat a large language model used as an evaluator (an "LLM-as-judge") as a measurement instrument and report its psychometric properties. Given a judge and a set of human-labeled examples, 'yourhonor' reports chance-corrected agreement between the judge and humans with bootstrap confidence intervals: Cohen's kappa (Cohen 1960) doi:10.1177/001316446002000104 , Krippendorff's alpha (Hayes and Krippendorff 2007) doi:10.1080/19312450709336664 , and Gwet's AC1 (Gwet 2008) doi:10.1348/000711006X126600 and weighted AC2 (Gwet 2014, ISBN:978-0970806284). It also reports human-human reliability when several raters are supplied, per-class error intervals, structured paired bias probes and test-retest stability. Explicit acceptance policies turn evidence into conservative decisions, and versioned artifacts support portable aggregate audit review. It complements the 'ellmer' and 'vitals' evaluation stack: it does not run evaluations, it measures the judge that scores them.
